topics.title: Skin Overview
topics.body:
New Horizon — v5.5

New Horizon is the flagship SnapSmack skin. It is a high-contrast dark-mode theme built for photographers who want maximum control over presentation. Every visual element — framing, typography, spacing, wall physics — is configurable through the Pimpotron (Smooth Your Skin).

Key Features

  • Floating Gallery support — fully interactive 3D drag-and-drop wall with configurable physics, shadows, and typography.
  • Three archive layouts — Square (uniform grid), Cropped (constrained aspect ratio), and Masonry (justified rows preserving full aspect ratio).
  • Five image frame styles — Revival Double, Classic White, Gallery Mat, Minimal Bevel, and Obsidian.
  • Full JS library — lightbox, keyboard navigation, justified layout engine, and footer animations.
  • Dropcap support — three styles (None, Simple Bold, Tactical Block) for decorative first letters in content.
  • Extensive typography controls — separate font, size, and spacing settings for headers, body content, and footers.

topics.title: Image Framing
topics.body:
Image Frame Styles

New Horizon offers five distinct frame styles for single-image views and a separate set for archive thumbnails. Configure these in Smooth Your Skin under "Vertical Locks".

Single Image Frames

  • Revival Double — a double-border frame with a thin inner rule and a heavier outer border. Elegant and classical.
  • Classic White — a clean white border that acts as digital matting. Works well with both colour and black-and-white photography.
  • Gallery Mat — simulates a traditional gallery mat with a wider border and subtle depth. The most museum-like option.
  • Minimal Bevel — a thin single border with a slight bevel effect. Understated and modern.
  • Obsidian — a dark frame that blends with the background, making the image appear to float. Best for high-key or bright images.

Archive Frames

Archive thumbnails have their own frame options, typically simpler: thin border, medium border, shadow, heavy shadow, gallery mat, or none. These are set separately because what works at full size often doesn't work at thumbnail scale.

topics.title: Floating Gallery Settings
topics.body:
Floating Gallery Configuration

The floating gallery is a 3D interactive experience unique to skins that support it. Engine settings live in Global Vibe; visual settings stay in Smooth Your Skin.

Engine Settings (Global Vibe)

  • Reflection — toggle a below-tile reflection effect (Chromium/Safari).
  • Scroll Friction (0.80–0.99) — controls how quickly the wall decelerates after dragging. Low values feel like ice; high values feel heavy and controlled.
  • Drag Weight (0.5–5.0) — multiplier for drag resistance.
  • Gallery Link — show or hide the nav link.

Visual Settings (Smooth Your Skin)

  • Wall Background — the colour behind the tiles. Pure black by default.
  • Text Colour — title text that appears on hover.
  • Shadow Colour & Intensity — the glow or shadow behind each tile.
  • Font — the typeface used for tile titles on the wall.

topics.title: Typography
topics.body:
Typography Controls

New Horizon provides separate typography settings for different areas of the site.

Header

  • Font Family — the typeface for the site header/title area.
  • Font Size — range from small to large.

Content & Static Pages

  • Heading Font — used for h1, h2, h3 in static pages and descriptions.
  • Body Font — the main reading font for paragraph text.
  • Line Height (1.0–3.0) — vertical spacing between lines.
  • Letter Spacing (-2 to 10px) — horizontal spacing between characters.

Footer

  • Footer Font — typically a smaller or lighter weight for credits and metadata.
  • Footer Font Size — independent of other sizes.

Font Library

SnapSmack ships with a curated font library. The available fonts depend on what's installed in assets/fonts/. Each font has a license file in the licenses/ directory.

topics.title: Blogroll Display
topics.body:
Blogroll Display Settings

Configure how the blogroll page looks in Smooth Your Skin under "Blogroll".

Options

  • Columns (1–3) — how many columns the peer list displays in.
  • Max Width — constrains the blogroll container width.
  • Column Gap — spacing between columns.
  • Show Description — toggle visibility of peer descriptions.
  • Show URL — toggle visibility of peer website URLs.

topics.title: Likes, Reactions & Comments
topics.body:
Community Features

SnapSmack ships a built-in community system: likes, emoji reactions, and comments — all self-hosted on your own server, no third-party tracking or login walls.

Community Dock

A floating action button appears on every page. Tap it to expand the dock, which reveals a like button and a reaction picker (up to 6 emoji). Visitors can react without creating an account. Dock position (bottom-left or bottom-right) and the active reaction set are configured in Admin > Community Settings.

Comments

Comments appear below each image. To leave a comment, visitors create a free community account directly on your site — no email confirmation required, no third-party auth. Once logged in, their display name appears on all their comments. Approve or reject comments from Admin > Manage.

Admin Controls

Go to Admin > Community Settings to toggle likes, reactions, and comments independently; choose the active reaction set; enable or disable the thumbs-down reaction; set rate limits; and configure email notifications for new comments.
